Hi Morgan — attaching a short, SIG-friendly breakdown below and the network diagram. I'm keeping each item tight so you can paste into the SIG fields directly.

Hosted (Redwood SaaS) — summary for SIG:
- Ownership: Redwood operates the control plane and inference runtime; customers use the hosted API.
- Data residency: customers select region (multi-region offering); data at-rest encryption is enabled and keys are managed by Redwood KMS for hosted by default.
- Access controls: Redwood employee access is governed by RBAC, documented just-in-time (JIT) approval workflows, and audited in our access logs.
- Evidence: SOC2_report_2025.pdf (covers hosted service within scope), sample access audit extract (redacted), and hosting architecture diagram.

Dedicated (reserved capacity) — summary for SIG:
- Ownership: compute is reserved for a single customer logically isolated at the runtime layer; control plane still operated by Redwood (optional dedicated control plane in some contracts).
- Data residency: Dedicated can be pinned to customer-preferred regions; data-at-rest encryption uses either Redwood-managed or customer-managed keys (KMIP/KMS option).
- Access controls: Redwood access to Dedicated environments is limited by environment-level ACLs and requires elevated approvals (JIT + documented change ticket).
- Evidence: network_diagram_vpc.png (example of dedicated pool segmentation), ACL policy excerpts, configuration profile showing KMS key ownership.

Private / VPC / On-prem — summary for SIG:
- Ownership: customer-managed control plane and/or on-premise deployment; Redwood provides the software and optionally remote support.
- Data residency & control: customer retains full control; keys are customer-managed (HSM/KMS) and data does not traverse Redwood-managed services unless explicitly configured.
- Access controls: Redwood employee access can be fully restricted (support via customer-managed bastion or VPN) or enabled under narrow, auditable procedures per contract.
- Evidence: signed deployment diagram, optional support access process document, and sample contract clause for access restrictions.

Notes on telemetry & model data: by default Redwood does not use customer prompt data to train public models. We offer an explicit telemetry opt-out for customers requiring absolute separation.

I've attached: network_diagram_vpc.png, SIG_answer_draft.docx (first pass). Let us know which SIG row IDs you want us to paste into directly.

Cheers,

Morgan and Liam — answering each point directly and attaching the remaining artifacts.

1) Dedicated: Redwood engineers do not have unfettered root access to customer VMs. Access model:
- Access is role-scoped and requires an approved access ticket (our ITSM) with JIT timebox and rationale.
- All sessions use our audited jump hosts and SSO with MFA; commands are session-logged and stored in tamper-evident audit logs.
- We can provide a redacted sample access log extract and an ACL policy excerpt (see attachments).

2) Private/on-prem no-access option: yes — we offer a contractable "zero-access" support mode. In this model:
- Redwood operates in advisory/support role only; all support actions require customer-owned bastions or runbooks executed by customer staff.
- For critical incidents customers may opt to enable temporary access under strict JIT approval; every enablement is logged and requires both customer and Redwood approval.
- Evidence: sample support runbook and signed deployment diagram (attached).

3) Sample procurement clause (redlined snippet):
"Redwood shall not access Customer Data in Dedicated or Private/VPC environments except pursuant to a documented, time-limited support request approved by Customer. Any access will be performed under Customer-defined controls, logged, and limited to the minimum privileges required. Redwood shall not exfiltrate Customer Data and shall comply with Customer data handling and retention requirements. Emergency access may be granted only when mutually agreed and will be subject to post-access audit."

Additional notes:
- SOC2_report_2025.pdf covers our hosted SaaS environment and the operational controls we reference above. For Dedicated deployments that remain under Redwood control (control plane managed by Redwood), many of the same operational controls apply; for on-prem Private deployments the SOC2 scope depends on whether Redwood manages any part of the control plane — we document scope on a per-deal basis.
- Telemetry: customers can opt out of prompt-level telemetry; stored telemetry used for platform reliability is aggregated and accessible only to engineers with audit-logged access.

Attachments included: SOC2_report_2025.pdf, redacted_access_log_sample.txt, support_runbook_sample.pdf, DocuSign_SLA_Amendment_Link.txt

If you'd like, we can paste the finalized text directly into your SIG spreadsheet.
